## (A) Research question & operationalized hypotheses

**Research question.** *Will BAdam achieve better performance on zero-shot math benchmarks compared to LoRA when finetuning Llama 3-70B on MathInstruct?*

**Definition of "better".** The headline question is answered under **three pre-registered framings**, so the conclusion cannot be cherry-picked from a single test:

| Framing | Definition on the paired-difference Δ = mean(BAdam) − mean(LoRA) across 5 seeds | Headline verdict |
|---|---|---|
| (i) **Superiority** | Δ > 0 with one-sided paired t-test (or Wilcoxon if normality violated) and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.05 on **≥ 1 primary benchmark** (GSM8K or MATH). | BAdam is **better** if (i) holds. |
| (ii) **Non-inferiority** | \|Δ\| ≤ **1.0 percentage point** with two-sided corrected p > 0.05 on **both primary benchmarks**. Margins are pre-registered; 1pp is justified by the literature's 5-seed paired-std at LoRA r≈32 reported on GSM8K/MATH (typical σ_paired ≈ 0.4–0.7pp). | BAdam is **at least as good** if (i) fails but (ii) holds. |
| (iii) **Pareto (accuracy vs peak memory)** | Report (accuracy, peak GPU memory) per cell. BAdam is **Pareto-better** than LoRA on a benchmark if its accuracy lower 95 % CI bound ≥ LoRA's *and* its peak memory is strictly lower; otherwise we report its Pareto position. | Memory-efficient BAdam claim honored. |

The BAdam paper's headline thesis makes framing (i) the most aggressive hypothesis on the harder MATH benchmark and framing (iii) the headline claim on memory. Framings (i)/(ii) are reported on primary benchmarks; framing (iii) is reported on all four.

**Operationalized hypotheses per benchmark** (formally pre-registered as the alternative for the paired test):

* H_a (GSM8K, BAdam-Full vs LoRA-r32): Δ > 0 with corrected p < 0.05.
* H_a (MATH, BAdam-Full vs LoRA-r32): Δ > 0 with corrected p < 0.05.
* H_a (GSM8K, BAdam-Block-LoRA-r32 vs LoRA-r32 [fairness mirror]): Δ > 0 with corrected p < 0.05 (per (i)); non-inferiority per (ii) is the secondary claim.
* H_a (SVAMP; AQuA-RAT): same three framings, reported but framed as secondary (no primary claim of superiority is made).

**Primary cells.** Two cells carry the headline claims:

* **Cell P (primary):** LoRA(r=32, α=64, all-linear) vs **BAdam-Full** (the BAdam paper's headline memory-efficient *full*-parameter SFT). This is the "spirit of the question" — same compute envelope, different parameterization.
* **Cell F (fairness-mirror, secondary cell reported alongside P):** LoRA(r=32, α=64, all-linear) vs **BAdam-Block-LoRA(r=32)** — trainable scalar parameter count matched within 1× (414.2M vs 414.2M); differs from LoRA only in (a) the parameter update is restricted per active block and (b) optimizer state cycling. This isolates "is block-wise update dynamics the lever?" from "does full-parameter training matter?".

Both cells are reported for all three framings.

## (B) Materials

### B.1 Model

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Subject model | `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70B` (the **base / pretrained / non-Instruct** checkpoint) |
| Precision | **bf16** for all frozen weights and forward/backward; **fp32 adapters** for LoRA / BAdam-Block-LoRA; **fp32 master + bf16 param** for full-param blocks in BAdam-Full |
| Training regime | Standard causal-LM next-token prediction with teacher-forcing on the MathInstruct response (prompt tokens masked in loss) |
| Tokenizer | the model's own BPE (tiktoken-backed in HF `transformers`); pad token = the dedicated `<|reserved_special_token_…|>` if none set; **no chat-template tokens** are added at train or eval because the base model is not chat-tuned |
| License / gating access | Llama-3 Community License; HF gated model — assumed **access granted** for design-only purposes; verification required before execution |

### B.2 Dataset

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Training data | **TIGER-Lab/MathInstruct** (Yue et al., 2023) — combined instruction-response set from 13 math-reasoning sources, ~262K total |
| HF path | `TIGER-Lab/MathInstruct` |

| **Primary condition** | **Stratified 80K subsample** preserving the 13-source proportions; trained for **2 epochs** (≈ 160K example passes) |
| **Dev split** | Held-out 2K examples from MathInstruct train, sampled *before* any contamination check on benchmarks; used for early-stop and dev-loss tracking only (no test items) |
| **Scale-robustness condition** | Full 262K, 1 epoch; reported as a secondary arm to confirm (i) does not reverse at scale |

| Item | Value |
|---|---|

| Frameworks | DeepSpeed **ZeRO-3** + **gradient checkpointing** + **bf16 mixed precision** |
| BAdam-Full cell | Requires **upper bound** (3–4× H100) with **8-bit AdamW** (`bitsandbytes.optim.AdamW8bit`) for the active block's optimizer state |

### B.4 Unknown-but-used assets (no execution implied)

We **only describe behaviorally**; we do not assume their internal correctness:
* The `peft` LoRA implementation (Hu et al., 2021 re-impl) ✓ in `peft.LoraConfig`.
* The BAdam implementation, referenced as Luo et al. 2024 (paper): block-wise AdamW with CPU-offload/rotation of inactive-block optimizer state. We require that the implementation expose: (i) block count `B`, (ii) `warmup_steps_before_rotation`, (iii) the rotation schedule, (iv) per-block activation bf16. Cross-checked once via a 1B smoke test before the 70B run; if behavior deviates from paper, design is held and a new pre-registration is written.

## (C) Methods

### C.1 Baseline arm — LoRA (PEFT)

```
LoRA config         : r ∈ {16, 32, 64} ; α = 2r ; dropout = 0.05
Trainable targets   : all linear projections
                       {q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj,
                        gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj}
                       in every Transformer block (80 layers)
Frozen              : embed_tokens, LM head, RMSNorm, all base linear weights
Optimizer           : AdamW(β=(0.9, 0.999), wd=0) — applies only to adapters
LR schedule         : linear warmup 3% of total → cosine to 0
Peak LR search      : {1e-5, 2e-5, 5e-5}; 1 seed per cell; chosen = lowest dev loss;
                       threshold:   |Δdev_loss| < 2% → pick smaller LR;
                                   otherwise pick the LR with min dev loss.
Frozen headline LR : chosen LR frozen for the 5-seed headline run.
Headline            : r=32, α=64 (414.2 M trainable scalar params — see computation below)
Sensitivities       : r=16 (207.1 M), r=64 (828.4 M)
```

**Trainable-parameter count derivation (used for budget matching):** with Llama-3-70B hidden=8192, kv_heads=8 (head_dim=128), intermediate=28672, 80 layers, the all-linear target module total is ≈ 68.45 B trainable target params (Q+O = 8192² × 2 per layer = 134.2 M; K+V = 8192 × 1024 × 2 per layer = 16.8 M; MLP = 3 × 8192 × 28672 per layer ≈ 704.6 M; total per layer ≈ 855.6 M; ×80 ≈ 68.45 B). LoRA adds `r × (in+out)` per module per layer; summing over all seven modules per layer × 80 layers yields **414.2 M at r=32**, 207.1 M at r=16, 828.4 M at r=64.

### C.2 Primary arm — BAdam-Full (full-parameter block-wise Adam)

```
Block partition    : 10 blocks; 8 contiguous Transformer layers per block
Rotation schedule  : cyclic, block index advances by 1 every optimizer step
Warmup             : step-wise warm-up of LR for 3% of total optimizer steps;
                       then 1 epoch (sequential) of "warm-up the first block to convergence" before rotation begins (matches paper's 1-epoch pre-rotation warmup)
Optimizer          : AdamW(β=(0.9, 0.999), wd=0); 8-bit AdamW (bitsandbytes)
                     for the *active* block's optimizer state only;
                     inactive-block optimizer states are CPU-offloaded
Param representation: per-parameter master copy in fp32 + bf16 weight buffer
Trainable          : all 70B parameters (excluding embed_tokens and LM head which are frozen throughout)
LR schedule        : linear warmup 3% of total → cosine to 0
Peak LR search     : {1e-5, 2e-5}    (tightened vs LoRA: per paper intuition
                                       that full-parameter SFT needs smaller LR)
Headline           : LR chosen by dev-loss; frozen for 5-seed headline run
```

### C.3 Fairness-mirror arm — BAdam-Block-LoRA

```
Baseline block part.: 10 contiguous layer blocks, 8 layers/block
Rotation + warmup   : identical to BAdam-Full
Trainable targets   : the LoRA adapters inside the active block only; at every
                       step, only that block's adapters receive gradients; the
                       inactive blocks' adapters are forward-passed and
                       skipped from optimizer state
Optimizer           : AdamW(β=(0.9, 0.999), wd=0); fp32 (small)
LoRA config         : identical r, α, dropout to the *paired* LoRA cell
Param-budget match  : LoRA(r=32) all-linear: 414.2 M trainable;
                       BAdam-Block-LoRA(r=32): 414.2 M trainable (exact match);
                       BAdam-Block-LoRA(r=16, r=64) as sensitivities
                       (≤ 2× budget rule ⇒ r=32 is the headlined choice)
```

### C.4 Alignment variables (locked)

| Aligned variable | How it is matched | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Total tokens seen | identical (same packed-sequence bucketing: pack to 4096 tokens, first-fit; 80K examples ≈ 10K packed sequences; 2 epochs ≈ 20K seqs) | drives compute |
| Optimizer steps | identical | batch size fixed at 2 micro × 4 grad-accum = 8 effective batch per "packed sequence" = effective token batch = 32 768 |
| Effective batch | identical | 32 768 tokens/step; 80K condition → ~625 steps/epoch × 2 epochs ≈ 1 250 steps |
| Wall-clock-per-token | identical (same ZeRO-3, same activation checkpointing, same bf16 precision); BAdam uses 8-bit Adam where LoRA uses fp32 | reported measured wall-clock per cell as Pareto covariate |
| Data order | same per-seed seed-init RNG; same shuffled indices fed to both paired cells | ensures *paired* random effects |
| Tokenization | identical tokenizer call, identical prompt template | no leakage from prompt variance |
| Init of trainable params | stable seed init, frozen base seed | matched |
| Eval template / extractor / decoding | identical across cells | matched |
| Peak GPU memory | **not** matched — measured as the Pareto covariate (this is exactly what (iii) reports) |  |

**What is not matched (intentionally).**

* Peak LR is allowed to differ *between methods* (each method's LR is tuned to its own dev loss within {1e-5, 2e-5, [5e-5 only for LoRA]}); once chosen, LR is frozen across methods for headline comparisons.
* Trainable parameter count is *intentionally* imbalanced between Cell P's two arms (414M vs 70B) because that is the question; it is *intentionally* balanced within Cell F (414M vs 414M).

### C.5 Training schedule (locked)

```
Training objective  : causal LM NLL on response tokens (prompt masked via labels=-100)
Sequence handling   : pack to 4096-token sequences; positional + causal masks built
                       correctly with attention island isolation across documents (flash-attn var-len)
Dropout             : adapter dropout 0.05 (LoRA, BAdam-Block-LoRA);
                       0 (full-param blocks have no per-layer dropout in BAdam-Full —
                          paper convention)
Gradient clipping   : global L2-norm 1.0
Mixed precision     : bf16 forward + bf16 backward; fp32 master weights where used;
                       8-bit AdamW for active block in BAdam-Full
Checkpointing       : activation checkpointing on every Transformer block
Checkpoint cadence  : every 250 steps; keep best-3 by dev loss; final = best-by-dev
Early-stop          : patience 3 evals (each eval = 1/4 epoch step on dev slice)
Total tokens        : 80K condition × ~410 avg tokens × 2 epochs ≈ 65.6 M tokens
                       (exact token count recorded at run time and reused for full-262K scale arm)
```

## (D) Evaluation

### D.1 Benchmark panel

| Tier | Benchmark | Size | Task | Primary metric |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Primary** | GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) | 1 319 test | grade-school word-problems, free-form | exact-match @ greedy |
| **Primary** | MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021) | 5 000 test | competition math, free-form with `\boxed{}` | exact-match via MATH-grader equivalence (`minervamath` or `math_verify`) |
| Secondary | SVAMP (Patel et al., 2021) | 300 test | arithmetic word-problem variations | exact-match @ greedy |
| Secondary | AQuA-RAT (Ling et al., 2017) | 254 test | algebra, multiple-choice A–E | option-accuracy (single letter) |

AQuA-RAT is **dropped from primary analyses if its contamination rate exceeds 2 %** (resolves U6). It remains in secondary. SVAMP is similarly audited.

### D.2 Prompting

* **Single canonical template (frozen).** For all benchmarks, all seeds, all cells:

  ```
  Q: <question>
  A:
  ```

* The base model is **not chat-tuned**, so no chat-template tokens are inserted. Sensitivity at eval (a separate secondary table) repeats evaluation under the MathInstruct SFT format:

  ```
  <|begin_of_text|>Instruction: <question>
  Response:
  ```

* **Zero-shot.** No in-context examples. Few-shot = 0 (this is required by the research question).

### D.3 Decoding

* Greedy decoding, `do_sample=False`, `temperature=0.0`.
* `max_new_tokens = 512` for MATH; `256` for GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA.
* Stop on EOS or `\n\nQ:` (whichever comes first).
* No length penalty; no repetition penalty.

### D.4 Answer extraction (identical across cells)

A two-stage deterministic extractor:

1. **`\boxed{…}` regex** → first match used (MATH primary path). Multi-box collapse by chosen-order.
2. **`The answer is X`** regex → fallback (covers a subset of GSM8K / SVAMP that includes verbal answer phrases).
3. **Last-number-in-string** fallback (GSM8K / SVAMP).
4. **Letter regex `\(?[A-E]\)?`** for AQuA: pick the last matched option.

The same extractor is run on both LoRA and BAdam outputs; outputs are normalized via Unicode normalization and `\frac{a}{b}` → `a/b` standardization before exact-match scoring (MATH only).

### D.5 Contamination gate (resolves U6)

1. **Construction.** For each candidate `{test item, prompt + expected answer}` and each MathInstruct *train* example, compute:
    * 25-gram character overlap (with whitespace tokens) on the prompt string;
    * full-string match `prompt == train.string`;
    * answer-token Jaccard ≥ 0.9 on answer-bearing sub-strings.
2. **Drop rule.** Drop any test item **before scoring** if any one of (a) ≥25-gram prompt overlap, (b) full-string match on prompt, (c) answer Jaccard ≥ 0.9.
3. **Reporting.** Per benchmark: contamination rate = (dropped) / (original test size) reported with the headline numbers.
4. **Hard gate.** AQuA-RAT → if contamination rate > 2 %, AQuA is moved from secondary to *excluded* (reported only as a footnote). Same rule for SVAMP.
5. **GSM8K / MATH test sets** are held-out by construction in their original releases; expected contamination ≈ 0.

### D.6 What gets logged

Per run, per benchmark: per-item prompt, response, extracted answer, gold answer, exact-match verdict, tokens-decoded, seconds. Saved as a CSV/JSONL log; aggregated into per-seed accuracy and per-cell accuracy tables.

## (E) Statistical analysis plan

### E.1 Sample size and pairing

* `n_seeds = 5` per cell (default; 3 if budget-constrained, with pre-registration update).
* Each seed `s` produces paired observations `(LoRA_s, BAdam_s)` trained on the identical seed-init token stream. Differences are computed cell-wise.

### E.2 Test statistic

For each benchmark B and Cell P or F:

1. Compute Δ_s(B) = accuracy_s(BAdam, B) − accuracy_s(LoRA, B) for s = 1..5.
2. **Normality check** on Δ_s(B) via Shapiro–Wilk. If p ≥ 0.05 → use **paired t-test** (two-sided for non-inferiority, one-sided for superiority). If p < 0.05 → fall back to **Wilcoxon signed-rank** (two-sided for non-inferiority, one-sided for superiority).
3. **Effect size:** **Cohen's d_z** = mean(Δ_s(B)) / SD(Δ_s(B)).
4. **Confidence interval:** **BCa bootstrap** on Δ_s(B) with B = 10 000 resamples, 95 % CI.
5. **Multiple-comparisons correction:** within each cell, the four benchmarks are corrected by **Holm–Bonferroni** at α = 0.05.

### E.3 Acceptance verdicts (all three framings)

* **(i) Superiority.** BAdam wins on a benchmark if Δ̂ > 0 **and** corrected p < 0.05 (one-sided). Headline answer (i) = at least one primary benchmark wins.
* **(ii) Non-inferiority** (margin m = 1 pp = 0.01). BAdam is non-inferior on B if |Δ̂ − 0| ≤ m and the **two-sided** corrected test p > 0.05 (i.e., we cannot reject the null that |Δ| > m). Headline (ii) = both primary benchmarks meet it.
* **(iii) Pareto.** Plot accuracy (95 % CI) vs peak GPU memory per cell, per primary benchmark. BAdam is Pareto-better on B iff its lower-CI bound ≥ LoRA's accuracy **and** its peak memory is strictly lower; otherwise report Pareto position.

### E.4 Pre-registration

Before any training: write the pre-registration document listing
* all locked hyperparameters (LR, schedule, batch, BCa iterations, Holm family size),
* the exact extractor / decoder / prompt template,
* the contamination rule and per-benchmark drop counts,
* the seed list,
* the three pre-registered framings and their decision thresholds.

Commit the pre-registration (hash-pinned) before unlocking training. Any later change re-opens pre-registration and is reported with explicit `deviation` tags.

## (H) Threats to validity

* **Contamination.** GSM8K/MATH test sets are held out, but MathInstruct was *built from various training sets*; the audit per §D.5 with a 2 % hard gate is the primary mitigation. AQuA and SVAMP are uplift-prone; their possible exclusion is pre-registered.
* **Prompt sensitivity.** A single canonical template (no chat tokens) is used to remove prompt variance. A sensitivity secondary table repeats evaluation under the MathInstruct SFT format; if results disagree, the template used to train (and the base model's non-instruction-tuned nature) is the most plausible cause and is reported as such.
* **Single-model, single-tokenizer.** Llama-3-70B base is one model; generalization to, e.g., Mistral, Qwen, or Llama-3.1-Instruct is not tested in this design. We do not claim cross-model generalization.
* **MathInstruct source overlap with SVAMP / AQuA.** Even after the contamination drop rule, residual topical / structural overlap can favor methods that better memorize the train distribution. Mitigation: we report SVAMP/AQuA as secondary only, and we report SVAMP/AQuA exclusion rate on the headline table.
* **Seed variance at 70B PEFT scale.** With ~10 8 -bit trainable parameters (LoRA-r16) to ~10 9 trainable parameters (LoRA-r32), gradient noise on a 41M-token training budget is the dominant source of variance. 5-seed paired design is the primary mitigation; fallback at 3 seeds is documented.
* **Method-implementation deviation, not method itself.** BAdam-Full's per-step behavior is sensitive to block-count, rotation policy, and offload scheduling. We adopt the paper's settings (U3) but acknowledge the implementation we use is **not the paper's reference implementation quirk-free**. Smoke test on a 1B model mitigates the most likely failure modes.
* **LR-asymmetry.** Cell P (BAdam-Full) and Cell P (LoRA) use method-specific peak LRs tuned on dev. This is the most defensible fairness convention in PEFT literature, but is an explicit axis on which cells differ; we report the chosen LRs in the headline.
* **Pareto measurement.** Peak memory is what is reported; throughput (tokens/sec) is reported separately. The two Pareto axes answer slightly different sub-claims of the BAdam paper, and we report them as such; we do **not** recompute accuracy under any "matched memory" capping.
* **Skill vs. memorization.** MATH's free-form answer extraction honors the boxed-expression convention, but a model that emits verbose prose can fail extraction the same way; the extractor is identical across cells, so the differential effect cancels but absolute numbers may be lower than leader-board numbers from differently-prompted systems.

---

## (I) Reporting plan

**Headline table A.1 — Accuracies per benchmark (mean ± std across seeds; primary condition).**

| Method | GSM8K | MATH | SVAMP | AQuA-RAT (or excluded) | Peak GPU mem |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LoRA-r32 (headline) | mean ± std | … | … | … | X GB |
| BAdam-Full | … | … | … | … | Y GB |
| (Δ, 95% BCa CI, p_holm) | per col | per col | per col | per col | n/a |

**Headline table A.2 — Paired-difference verdicts.**

| Benchmark | Δ̂ (BAdam − LoRA) | BCa 95 % CI | Cohen's d_z | corrected p | Verdict (i) sup | Verdict (ii) NI | Verdict (iii) Pareto |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Cell P and Cell F each have one row per benchmark.

**Figure plan.**
* **Fig. 1** — per-benchmark paired-difference forest plot (Cell P, primary condition) with 95 % BCa CIs and the 1pp non-inferiority band.
* **Fig. 2** — Pareto plot: accuracy on MATH vs peak GPU memory, one marker per (cell, seed), color-coded by method.
* **Fig. 3** — training curves (dev loss and benchmark accuracy on a held-out 500-example MATH slice) over the 1 250-step run, averaged across seeds; shaded = 95 % BCa band.

**Sensitivity table A.3.**
* Sensitivity (`r = 16`, `r = 32`, `r = 64`) of LoRA and BAdam-Block-LoRA on the two primary benchmarks; same statistics.

**Robustness table A.4.**
* Full-262K condition, LoRA-r32 vs BAdam-Full on GSM8K and MATH (3 seeds); only used to cross-check (i)/(ii) does not flip sign at scale.

**Side table A.5** — per-benchmark contamination rate and excluded item count.

**Verdict mapping to the research question** is reported as a single sentence per framing:

* (i) "BAdam **does better than** LoRA on the math benchmark {GSM8K | MATH | neither}" iff the one-sided corrected test on ≥ 1 primary benchmark passes.
* (ii) "BAdam is **at least as good as** LoRA on the math panel" iff both primary benchmarks pass the 1pp NI check.
* (iii) "BAdam is **a Pareto-improved fit** for this fine-tune" iff accuracy is non-inferior AND peak memory is strictly lower on at least one primary benchmark.
